source.author: Al Brooks
source.chapter_title: Trend Bars, Doji Bars, and Climaxes

conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode. Helpers: range(n) = high[n]-low[n]; body(n) = close[n]-open[n]; upperTail(n) = high[n]-max(open[n],close[n]); lowerTail(n) = min(open[n],close[n])-low[n]; avgRange(N) = average of range over the N bars ending at bar 1; medianBody(N) = median of abs(body) over the N bars ending at bar 1; tick = instrument minimum price move (structural constant); highest(x,N)[k] / lowest(x,N)[k] = extreme over N bars ending at bar k.

candidates.name: TrendBar
candidates.quote: If there is a body, then the close trended away from the open and the bar is a trend bar.
candidates.description: Primitive: bar 0 is a bull trend bar, with a body that is at least a fraction of its range (a plainer, looser threshold than a 'strong' trend bar).
notes: ConsecutiveUpBars at consecutiveBars=1 is the bodyFraction=0 special case (any close above open); this adds the size threshold.
Chapter 7 (already mined) defines the same primitive with bodyFraction 0.6 as 'strong'; the dedup pass should merge these.

candidates.name: DojiBar
candidates.quote: If the body appears tiny or nonexistent on the chart, the bar is a doji; neither the bulls nor the bears controlled the bar, and the bar is essentially a one-bar trading range.
candidates.description: Primitive: bar 0 is a doji (nontrend) bar, its body a small fraction of its range. Direction-agnostic.
notes: Brooks: 'in trading, close is close enough,' explicitly rejecting a zero-tolerance definition (open == close) in favor of a small-fraction threshold.

candidates.name: ClimaxEndsOnBreakBar
candidates.quote: if there are three consecutive bull trend bars and then the next bar is a small bull trend bar with a prominent tail on the top, an inside bar, a doji, or a bear trend bar, then the climax ended with the three bull trend bars.
candidates.description: A run of climaxBars consecutive bull trend bars ended at bar 1, and bar 0 is not itself a same-strength bull trend bar (a pause, tailed bar, inside bar, doji, or bear bar broke the streak): the buy climax has ended, which gates fade/reversal setups.

complexity.reason: needs a persistent streak counter of consecutive same-direction trend bars

candidates.name: TrendingDojiRun
candidates.quote: if there is a series of dojis, each with a higher close and most with a high above the high of the prior bar and a low above the low of the prior bar, the market is displaying trending closes, highs, and lows, so a trend is in effect.
candidates.description: Context filter: the last runBars bars are all doji bars, but each has a higher close, high, and low than the one before it -- a trend is in effect despite the small bodies, permitting with-trend entries that a plain doji count would otherwise block.
candidates.pseudocode: for k in 0..runBars-1: DojiBar[k] && close[k] > close[k+1] && high[k] >= high[k+1] && low[k] >= low[k+1]

complexity.reason: fixed-offset pairwise comparisons across a small window

notes: Book example: 'four dojis in a row' each trending, ending in a bull reversal bar at a new swing low.

candidates.name: TrendBarBodyAboveRecentMedian
candidates.quote: The bulls can demonstrate stronger control by having the body be about the same size as or larger than that of the median body size over the past five or 10 bars.
candidates.description: Context filter: a bull trend bar's body is at least as large as the median absolute body size of the last N bars, a sign of stronger with-trend control.

complexity.reason: a median requires ordering the window's body sizes, more than a running average

notes: Brooks gives 'five or 10 bars'; 10 chosen as the default.

candidates.name: LargeTrendBarExhaustionBreakoutFilter
candidates.quote: If the bar is very large and especially if it develops in a trend, it might represent exhaustion or a one-bar false breakout that is trapping new bulls, only to reverse down in the next bar or two.
candidates.description: Block a with-trend breakout entry whose signal bar is abnormally large relative to recent bars (possible exhaustion / one-bar false-breakout trap).
notes: p90: 'an extremely large body after a protracted move or a breakout can represent an exhaustive, climactic end of a trend, and no trade should be taken until more price action unfolds.'

candidates.name: FailedBreakoutNoFollowThroughFade
candidates.quote: bar 6 was a strong bull trend bar that broke out of a line of dojis. However, there was no follow-through. The next bar extended one tick above the trend bar and then closed near its low.
candidates.description: Long side (the book's mirror image: a bear breakout that fails and closes strong): a bear trend bar made a new low versus the last priorBars bars, the next bar failed to extend more than a small tolerance below that low, and it closed in the upper part of its own range: buy above this bar, expecting the failed breakout to reverse.
candidates.pseudocode: TrendBar[1] && close[1] < open[1] && low[1] <= lowest(low, priorBars)[2] && low[0] >= low[1] - toleranceTicks * tick && (close[0] - low[0]) >= closeNearHighFraction * range(0)
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above this bar's high; the failed breakout bar becomes the signal bar

complexity.reason: lowest-over-window plus a multi-bar failed-breakout pattern

notes: Similar in spirit to T07-30 (outside-bar version, already mined) but works off a plain trend-bar breakout with no outside-bar requirement.

candidates.name: RequireSecondCounterTrendBarConfirmation
candidates.quote: An experienced trader would have needed follow-through in the form of a second or third bull trend bar before believing that the always-in trade had reversed to up.
candidates.description: Block treating a single trend bar against the established trend as a reversal signal; require at least confirmBars consecutive trend bars in the new direction before permitting an entry in that direction.
notes: p91: 'What they need to see is follow-through selling in the form of maybe just one more bear trend bar' -- the mirror-direction statement of the same idea.

candidates.name: AccumulatingCounterTrendBodiesPressure
candidates.quote: If bear bodies are starting to accumulate in a bull trend or trading range, it is a sign of selling pressure and the bears might soon be able to create a downtrend.
candidates.description: Context filter: at least K of the last N bars are bull trend bars, signaling building buying pressure that permits anticipatory long entries even against the prevailing trend.

complexity.reason: window count of a bar classification

notes: p236-240: signs of buying pressure in a bear trend also include lower tails and bull reversal bars at swing lows -- those are separate primitives, not folded in here.

candidates.name: ProtractedTrendClimacticReversalSetup
candidates.quote: Whenever a large bear trend bar forms in a bear trend that has gone on for 30 or more bars without much of a pullback, it often represents a sell vacuum and an exhaustive sell climax.
candidates.description: Long side (the book's bear-trend example): after a bear trend of at least minTrendBars bars with no pullback larger than pullbackMaxFraction of the move, a bar forms whose range is abnormally large versus recent bars: buy, expecting an exhaustive sell climax and reversal.
candidates.pseudocode: barsSinceTrendStart(bear) >= minTrendBars && maxPullbackFraction(minTrendBars) <= pullbackMaxFraction && range(0) >= climaxMultiple * avgRange(rangeLookback) && close[0] < open[0]
candidates.book_order_type: buy at the market as the bar closes, or above its high

complexity.reason: 'a trend that has gone on for 30+ bars without much pullback' needs a trend-length and pullback-size design decision, on top of the range comparison

notes: p104: the Figure 2.5 example has each bear body in the final spike progressively larger, reinforcing the climax read.

candidates.name: MinimumCorrectionAfterClimaxFilter
candidates.quote: Both are expecting a larger correction that should have at least two legs, last at least 10 bars, and poke a little above the moving average.
candidates.description: After a climactic reversal setup (T02-10) fires, block resuming the old trend direction (fading the correction) until at least minCorrectionBars bars and two legs have elapsed since the climax bar.

complexity.reason: needs leg counting anchored to a specific climax bar, on top of a simple bar count

candidates.name: MeasuredMoveProjectionTarget
candidates.quote: Bar 9 formed a two-bar reversal at a measured move down from bar 3 to bar 4 (measured moves are discussed in book 2).
candidates.description: For a long entered at a reversal from a bear spike, take profit when price reaches a measured move equal to the size of the initial spike (swing high to swing low), projected up from the entry.
candidates.book_order_type: limit sell at the measured-move target

complexity.reason: spikeHighPrice/spikeLowPrice need swing-pivot detection to identify the initial spike being measured

notes: Full treatment is deferred to book 2 per the text; recorded here since the mechanism (project the spike's size from the reversal point) is a concrete, if pivot-dependent, target rule.

candidates.name: OpenNearBarExtremeStrength
candidates.quote: Additional signs of strength are discussed in another section and include the open being on or near the low, the close on or near the high
candidates.description: Context filter: a bull trend bar's open sits near its own low (little to no lower wick before the up-move began), a sign of strength.

candidates.name: CloseAboveRecentClosesAndHighsStrength
candidates.quote: the close at or above the closes and highs of several prior bars, the high above the high of one or more prior bars
candidates.description: Context filter: this bar's close is at or above both the highest close and the highest high of the last N bars -- a stronger with-trend signal than a plain new high.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] >= highest(close, N)[1] && close[0] >= highest(high, N)[1]

candidates.name: SmallTailsStrength
candidates.description: Context filter: the bar's upper and lower tails are both small relative to its range -- a direction-agnostic sign of a decisive (strong) trend bar.
candidates.pseudocode: upperTail(0) <= tailFraction * range(0) && lowerTail(0) <= tailFraction * range(0)

rejected.quote: Never be convinced of anything, and always be open to the possibility that the market will do the exact opposite of what you believe.
Subdividing bars with small bodies into a variety of subtypes like hanging man, hammer, or harami adds little to a trader.
rejected.reason: the book itself rejects naming bar subtypes; no distinct mechanical test beyond TrendBar/DojiBar

rejected.quote: Remember, all patterns are the result of computer algorithms, and computers have a huge speed advantage... traders should not trade against them.
rejected.reason: narrative about competing with algorithmic speed on lower time frames, not a bar-level condition on the traded chart

rejected.quote: The weak traders usually do the opposite. The weak bulls continue to sell at the lows as they get stopped out, and they buy at the highs as they become afraid that they are missing a new bull trend.
rejected.reason: descriptive trader psychology narrative, no bar-level test stated

rejected.quote: Remember, you can rarely be 60 percent certain of the market's direction, and that can quickly change to 50-50 or even 60 percent in the other direction.
rejected.reason: pure discretion about confidence level, not decidable from bars

rejected.quote: The chart on the left is a tick chart with each bar being 100 ticks... That is far too much information for a human to process reliably and then be able to place orders in a timely and accurate way.
rejected.reason: requires a different (tick-based, smaller time frame) chart's data than the strategy's own bars

chapter_summary: Chapter 2 defines the book's two fundamental bar classes (trend bar and doji) and builds the climax/vacuum/spike vocabulary on top of them: what makes a trend bar 'strong' (body size vs. median, open/close position, small tails), how a run of same-direction trend bars constitutes and ends a climax, how a run of trending dojis can still mark a trend, why isolated counter-trend trend bars need follow-through before being trusted, and how accumulating opposite-body pressure or an abnormally large trend bar after a long trend without pullback signals an approaching reversal. Produced the TrendBar/DojiBar primitives (chapter 7, already mined, redefines a stricter 'strong' TrendBar and reversal-bar primitives that should merge with these), several signal-bar-strength filters, a climax/pressure-accumulation family, and two hard/research-leaning setups (protracted-trend climactic reversal, measured-move target) that need trend-length and swing-pivot design decisions respectively.
